reviews.title: I don’t know they have achieved 4.8…
reviews.body:
I don’t know they have achieved 4.8 when they can’t meet what they advertised. Their website says if you order sims before the 3pm cut off then you will get your sims by next day delivery.

I ordered 2 sims Thursday 7am with a view to switching from o2 and I have yet to receive either of them. I have had on line chats with 2 agents and they haven’t been very helpful and are saying that standard delivery is 3 to 5 days which is counter to what it says on the website.

When I have transferred providers in the past I have always received sims by next day delivery. A friend of mine who was also with o2 decided to go with a different provider than me and he didn’t order till late in the afternoon and by midday he had received his sim. So if they can do it why can’t Lebara especially when they advertise that they do.

I am beginning to wander if I have made mistake in trying to transfer to Lebara I was swayed by the MSE site as the offer being a recommended one.

To add I have already been charged the first month on the day I ordered despite not receiving the sims to activate which I don’t think is right.

I have responded to the automated standard reply to negative reviews and received an email which is also an automated standard reply to say that responses are usually 5 to 7 days. Certainly not you would expect if they genuinely are wanting to resolve the issue.

reviews.title: Utterly shambolic onboarding
reviews.body:
Edit: email received from Lebara just this second

"Hello Paul,

 

Greetings from Lebara Customer Care.
We tried calling you on your registered Lebara number, but couldn’t reach you.
Please share an alternate number or a suitable time for a callback so we can assist you further and resolve your complaint." 

You can't call me on the number that you've disconnected!???? The shock, the horror, the ineptitude..

Original review:
Utterly shambolic onboarding: bungled number port, misinformation, and left without service
Returning to Lebara has proven to be an exercise in regret.
​The SIM card arrived promptly, and a number port was scheduled for 30 October. My previous provider disconnected my service on the morning of the 30th as anticipated, but the Lebara SIM failed to activate correctly. By 17:00, I received an email confirming the port was complete and instructing me to restart my device. Doing so yielded only data and SMS—voice calls remained entirely inoperative.
​Contact via web chat proved utterly futile. The agent offered disjointed, contradictory explanations, claiming simultaneously that the port could take until midnight and that disruptions were to be expected for 24 to 48 hours. Three days later, following further unhelpful chats, I resorted to calling customer service. I was informed a replacement SIM was required and was explicitly assured that an automated email warning my semi-functional SIM would be disconnected was erroneous. Unsurprisingly, that assurance was false: the SIM was promptly deactivated.
​I am now left with no mobile service whatsoever. To maintain minimal connectivity, I have had to purchase an interim SIM from another network at my own expense—which does not solve the issue of critical two-factor authentication (OTP) and urgent incoming calls tied to my ported number. To compound the absurdity, an adviser claimed the SIM in my hand was never linked to my number, despite it providing data and correctly displaying my ported number on my online account.
​Being told to simply "wait for a new SIM" encapsulates the sheer lack of competence and accountability displayed throughout this process. It has been an abysmal onboarding experience from the outset. I fully anticipate the standard boilerplate response promising that someone will "be in touch," though how that will be achieved given Lebara has stripped me of a functioning telephone line remains to be seen. Completely useless.

reviews.title: The court has now issued a CCJ against Lebara
reviews.body:
Following on from my last update regarding Lebara failure to adhere to the Ombudsman ruling the matter has taken a a further progression.

Lebara failed to respond to any correspondence from the Ombudsman and when the deadline expired for which they were required to complete the resolution, I wrote to the Ombudsman and Lebara to advise that I would be taking the matter to court. Lebara failed to respond as usual. The Ombudsman chased Lebara and they advised that they had completed all the requirements set out by the Ombudsman, however, in reality they had not.

I issued proceedings in the Small Claims Court for £135 to include court costs and the Particulars of Claims was duly sent to Lebara.  After the Particulars was issued and duly served, Lebara paid the £75 compensation awarded by the Ombudsman but failed to respond to the Claim. Following no response to the Court or myself, Judgement in Default was entered and Lebara now have a CCJ against them and have been ordered to pay the £60 remaining immediately.

Despite me contacting Lebara and Jean -Paul Patten (the so called Business Operations Director), response posted on here 22 September 2026, no one from Lebara has bothered to contact me. 

I now plan to seek a Third Party Order freezing all of Labara's bank accounts until such time as they pay the £60 plus the court costs for applying for the Third Party Order.
